chunks.article_title: Analysts Split on Banking Sector Outlook for Next Quarter
chunks.text: Investment banks remain divided on the outlook for Egyptian banking stocks heading into the next quarter. Naeem Brokerage raised its rating on CIB to "Overweight," citing strong net interest margins and improving asset quality, with a price target of EGP 92 per share. In contrast, EFG Hermes maintained a "Neutral" rating on the sector, warning that a potential interest rate cut later in the year could compress bank margins even as loan growth accelerates. EFG Hermes set a more conservative price target of EGP 78 for CIB. Both firms agree that asset quality has improved, with non-performing loan ratios across major banks falling to their lowest levels in three years. The disagreement centers primarily on interest rate trajectory and its impact on net interest income.

chunks.article_title: EGX30 Closes Higher as Banking Stocks Lead Gains
chunks.text: Cairo — The EGX30 index closed up 1.8% on Wednesday, driven primarily by gains in the banking sector. Commercial International Bank (CIB) rose 3.2%, while QNB Alahli gained 2.1%. Trading volume reached EGP 1.4 billion, roughly 15% above the 30-day average. Analysts attributed the rally to expectations that the Central Bank of Egypt will hold interest rates steady at its next meeting, reducing pressure on bank margins. The real estate sector lagged, with Talaat Moustafa Group down 0.9% amid concerns over rising construction costs. Foreign investors were net buyers for the third consecutive session, purchasing a net EGP 210 million in Egyptian equities.

chunks.article_title: Eastern Tobacco Reports 22% Jump in Quarterly Profit
chunks.text: Eastern Company (Eastern Tobacco) reported net profit of EGP 1.35 billion for the third quarter, up 22% year-over-year, beating analyst estimates of EGP 1.1 billion. Revenue grew 18% to EGP 4.2 billion, driven by higher domestic cigarette prices and stable export volumes to Gulf markets. The company's board approved an interim dividend of EGP 2.50 per share, payable next month. Management cited cost-control measures and a favorable currency environment as key drivers of margin expansion, with gross margin improving to 34% from 29% a year earlier. Eastern Tobacco shares rose 4.5% following the announcement, closing at EGP 18.90.

chunks.article_title: Egyptian Pound Stabilizes Near EGP 48.5 to the Dollar
chunks.text: The Egyptian pound traded relatively stable this week, hovering around EGP 48.5 per US dollar on the official interbank market, according to Central Bank of Egypt data. This follows several months of gradual depreciation earlier in the year. Economists note that improved foreign currency inflows from tourism revenue and remittances have eased pressure on the currency. The Central Bank's foreign reserves rose to $47.2 billion last month, up from $45.8 billion three months earlier. Market participants are watching closely for the Central Bank's upcoming monetary policy meeting, with most analysts expecting rates to remain unchanged at 27.25%.

chunks.article_title: FRA Introduces New Disclosure Rules for AI-Based Investment Tools
chunks.text: Egypt's Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA) issued new draft guidelines requiring any platform offering AI-generated investment recommendations to clearly disclose that such outputs do not constitute licensed financial advice, unless the provider holds an appropriate investment advisory license. The draft rules also require platforms to maintain audit logs of AI-generated recommendations for a minimum of five years, and to implement human review processes for any recommendation that could materially affect a retail investor's portfolio. The FRA opened a 45-day public comment period before the rules take effect. Industry participants, including several fintech platforms, are expected to submit feedback on implementation timelines and technical requirements.

chunks.article_title: Fintech Startup NileTech Files for EGX IPO, Targets EGP 800 Million
chunks.text: NileTech, a Cairo-based payments and digital lending startup, has filed for an initial public offering on the Egyptian Exchange, aiming to raise approximately EGP 800 million. The company plans to offer 25% of its shares to the public, valuing NileTech at roughly EGP 3.2 billion. Founded in 2019, NileTech processes over EGP 12 billion in annual payment volume and has expanded into consumer microloans over the past two years. The IPO proceeds are earmarked for expansion into Saudi Arabia and the UAE, as well as technology infrastructure upgrades. The offering is expected to open for subscription within six weeks, pending regulatory approval from the Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA).

chunks.article_title: Real Estate Stocks Under Pressure as Construction Costs Rise
chunks.text: Egyptian real estate developers are facing margin compression as steel and cement prices climbed 12% and 8% respectively over the past quarter. Talaat Moustafa Group, Palm Hills Developments, and Emaar Misr have all seen their stock prices decline between 3% and 7% over the past month. Despite the cost pressures, unit sales have remained resilient, with several developers reporting record pre-sales driven by installment-based payment plans that shield buyers from inflation. Palm Hills reported EGP 9.6 billion in new sales contracts for the quarter, up 14% year-over-year. Analysts remain divided: some see the sector as oversold given strong demand fundamentals, while others warn that margin pressure could persist into next year if input costs stay elevated.

chunks.article_title: Telecom Egypt Announces Special Dividend After Asset Sale
chunks.text: Telecom Egypt's board approved a special cash dividend of EGP 3.75 per share, funded by proceeds from the recent sale of a minority stake in its data center subsidiary. The total dividend payout amounts to approximately EGP 3.4 billion. The record date for the dividend is set for the 15th of next month, with payment to follow within two weeks. This is in addition to the company's regular annual dividend, which was already distributed earlier this year. Telecom Egypt shares gained 6.1% on the announcement, though some analysts cautioned that one-off dividends funded by asset sales should not be read as a signal of sustainably higher payouts going forward.
